::: {.intro-block}
My research develops practical, evidence-based ways to teach statistics and data science using authentic data. It connects three frameworks that move from *what* data we teach with, to *how* students work with it, to *how* they build understanding over time.
:::

::: {.section-head}
::: {.section-num}
01
:::
## Culturally Relevant Data (CRD)
::: {.rule}
:::
:::

::: {.intro-block}
Developed with Travis Weiland, **CRD** is a framework for selecting, creating, and using data that connects to students' lived experiences. Rather than treating datasets as neutral, CRD asks how data choices shape engagement, identity, and learning — and offers concrete guidance for instructors designing culturally responsive statistics courses.
:::

::: {.section-head}
::: {.section-num}
02
:::
## Extraction–Transformation–Visualization (ETV)
::: {.rule}
:::
:::

::: {.intro-block}
The **ETV model** structures data science instruction around a real workflow: **extracting** data from authentic sources (APIs, web tables, public datasets), **transforming** it into tidy, analyzable form, and **visualizing** it to surface insight. ETV gives students a repeatable mental model that mirrors professional practice.
:::

::: {.section-head}
::: {.section-num}
03
:::
## Library-Focused Method (LFM)
::: {.rule}
:::
:::

::: {.intro-block}
The **LFM** centers learning around the tools and libraries students will actually use, scaffolding fluency with packages and functions as a path to conceptual understanding — supported by the **SSVA** sequence (Summary Statistics → Visualization → Analysis).
:::
